hypothesis: The current research loop is being distorted by (1) diagnostics distributions not reflecting persisted event features (e.g., close_location_in_range, upper_wick_share) and (2) inability to join executed_trade events to realized trades for post-filter cohort analysis; fixing these will enable accurate falsification of future post-09:30 signal-quality mechanisms (including geometry and bearish-body confirmations).
mechanism: Implement two observability fixes: (A) Diagnostics generation should compute feature distributions directly from strategy_events.parquet columns (e.g., close_location_in_range, upper_wick_share) using finite-value counts, so distributions cannot show count=0 when the filter clearly used those features to reject 35,769 signals. (B) Persist a stable identifier (trade_id/event_id) into both strategy_events (for executed_trade rows) and trades.csv (and/or persist the realized entry timestamp used in trades.csv into executed_trade events) so we can join and compute PF/median_expectancy for pass/fail cohorts (especially post-09:30 where prior hypotheses focus).
dimension_novelty: Prior rounds attempted new post-09:30 signal-quality confirmations (close-vs-EMA, candle geometry) but were blocked by feature-scale anomalies and now a verified diagnostics aggregation bug + inability to join executed_trade events to trades for cohort testing. This thesis is not a parameter tweak; it is an observability/measurement primitive enabling falsifiable mechanism tests.
novel_connection: We now have direct evidence (round_19 analyst) that the candle-geometry features are computed and persisted correctly in strategy_events, but diagnostics distributions report zero counts, which can cause us to wrongly conclude features are missing/miscomputed and to iterate blindly. Fixing the measurement layer is a prerequisite to safely exploring signal-quality mechanisms without repeating the round-18 failure mode.
orthogonality_defense: Those theses change entry filtering rules; this thesis changes the strategy’s instrumentation so we can (a) correctly measure geometry feature distributions and (b) reliably join executed_trade events to realized trades for post-filter cohort evaluation. It enables future hypotheses across multiple dimensions rather than adjusting the existing gate.
falsification_or_alternative: If, after fixing diagnostics aggregation to read from strategy_events.parquet, geometry feature distributions still show count=0 or non-finite across large-N rejected cohorts, then the feature computation/persistence itself (not aggregation) is broken. If adding a stable join key still does not allow mapping executed_trade events to trades, then the issue is in event schema (missing entry timestamp/IDs) and needs a different linkage primitive.
why_existing_dimensions_do_not_fit: This is not about improving edge via entry/exit/regime/risk; it is about adding/fixing measurement primitives (diagnostics correctness + joinability) required to test those mechanisms without artifacts-driven false conclusions.
mechanism_family_definition: Changes that improve the correctness and granularity of strategy_events/diagnostics so that structural hypotheses (e.g., candle-geometry confirmation) can be validated with reliable pass/fail cohorts and without feature-reporting mismatches.
expected_reuse_across_future_theses: High: any future signal-quality/regime/risk hypothesis that depends on event-level features or rejection reasons will require trustworthy distributions and stable cohort linkage between events and executed trades.
evidence: Web (microstructure noise rationale for needing correct measurement): Roll (1984) shows bid–ask bounce can create mechanical negative serial dependence; to test reversal-vs-noise filters we need accurate feature measurement and cohort evaluation. https://www.acsu.buffalo.edu/~keechung/MGF743/Readings/Roll%201984.pdf

Data/code (round_19 analyst): diagnostics.json reports close_location_in_range.count=0 and upper_wick_share.count=0 while strategy_events.parquet has these columns populated for alert_close_location_reject rejected_signal rows (N=35,769); strategy.py::_compute_alert_bar_feature_arrays contains the correct formulas, so mismatch is diagnostics aggregation, not missing features.

expected_effects.rationale: Observability changes should not alter trading logic; windowed profitability should remain unchanged aside from negligible logging effects.
This is a measurement-only change; PF should remain the same, validating that we didn’t inadvertently change signal/exit behavior.

disqualifiers.name: behavior_change
disqualifiers.condition: profit_factor decreases by more than 1% versus the base experiment (measurement-only change should not move PF materially)

disqualifiers.name: diagnostics_mismatch_persists
disqualifiers.condition: After change, any feature used in a rejection reason (e.g., alert_close_location_reject) still has diagnostics distribution count < 90% of strategy_events finite count

required_diagnostics: diagnostics_feature_distribution_counts_vs_event_non_null_counts: for each distributed feature (close_location_in_range, upper_wick_share), report (diagnostics_count, strategy_events_non_null_count, strategy_events_finite_count) to catch future mismatches
event_trade_join_coverage: fraction of executed_trade events that can be linked to trades.csv (overall and by entry_bucket) after adding join key
post_filter_cohort_report: for any new rejection reason, report executed-trade PF/median_expectancy for pass vs fail cohorts when N>=50

requested_primitives: diagnostics pipeline: read feature distributions directly from strategy_events.parquet (not a reduced in-memory view) and count finite values
schema: add a stable event_id/trade_id written into both strategy_events (executed_trade rows) and trades.csv, or persist entry_timestamp in both for reliable joining
why_not_overfit: This is not an in-sample optimization; it is a correctness/traceability change. A diagnostics aggregation fix and a stable join key should generalize across datasets and is necessary for any subsequent mechanism testing to be scientifically falsifiable.
